optionalFindings.issue: The 'duplicate-id' selector control has more than one cause. Setting segments[1].id=1 breaks the strictly increasing id check. It also makes the expected name '...00000000000000000001.closed', which no longer matches the unchanged fileName '...00000000000000000002.closed'. The rejection therefore does not show that the monotonic/duplicate-id guard works by itself. 'active-first' (line 123) has the same problem, because the non-last expected name ends in '.active'. R2-01 isolated the guard in group-zero, but these two controls still are not isolated.
optionalFindings.recommendedFix: Optional: for duplicate-id, rename the closed member to the id-1 '.closed' name and record that fileName in the inventory, so only the id ordering fails. For active-first, either accept the combined failure and say so, or rename the member so that only the last-is-active rule triggers.

optionalFindings.issue: When the Windows symlink privilege is missing (winerror 1314), the skipped symlink control still counts toward the required total of 27 as {rejected: None, skipped: ...}. The documentation discloses this. However, the summary line printed on stdout reports selectorControls=27 without separating executed rejections from skips.
optionalFindings.recommendedFix: Optional: add an executed-versus-skipped selector count to the printed summary, or a skippedSelectorControls field to report.json, so the evidence audit does not have to search the controls array.

optionalDisposition.R3-O1: The duplicate-id and active-first cases are combined inconsistent-inventory rejection controls, not isolated mutation tests of individual guards. The guide states this limit.
optionalDisposition.R3-O2: Native arrays explicitly record unavailable Windows symlink privilege; final receipt separates configured cases, actual rejections and skips. The printed selectorControls value counts configured cases.
